Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 5aeba3ab65ea4689ec78c465cfdf430338b5450c
version info can be put into the flash hook, we don't need to do an additional lookup here.
we probably want to revisit this limit sometime as it is too relax for v2
why do we want to retry here? (I thought previous version we just fallback to v1, this should be a good indicator that installer does not support v2 or some other issues) and we should fallback fast.
nit: Uppercase for global and prefix like `GBMC_UPGRADE_METADATA`

`meta-google: gbmc-upgrade: Leverage metadata for download`

Describe why this is an advantage over using the full tarball download style. Also, avoid calling this V2 as that is meaningless outside of the design doc. Just use a description of the new download process.
I would avoid limiting here, move the limit stuff outside the download logic and apply it when the tmpdir is created. It doesn't make sense to change this every time.
In a URI it's called a `path`
`output` or similar as that's what curl and wget would call it.
You could just drop the message parameter and use the URL, we don't really need a separate message as the intention makes sense with surrounding context.
this makes is more readable and easier to understand to everyone not just us.

Don't we want to know what is being fetched? right now we don't even get the URI in the message. I'd argue if you really want to keep the message, you should still add the URI. But also, I believe it's always obvious what you are downloading purely by the URI.
Rename this to better describe how it works. `gbmc_upgrade_dl_metadata`
Just move this before the tmpdir is created so that it's not duplicated twice. It also doesn't make sense here because it will get executed twice right now.
You probably want to make the download function re-usable here. Probably you want one that just takes a URL, and a helper that calls it with $bootfile_url and `extract_metadata_first_match` easily.
Not sure if I follow, I agree that download is redundant, but I intentionally wanted to keep v1 untouched for reliability purposes on the field and clean up later after we gain confidence, thoughts?
Yeah, but you can sanely factor out these bits and test that they work by just not invoking the metadata download bit of the code.
Let me know your thoughts now, I think it's addressed now.
nit: Move this down to right above where it is set.
I think we still need the original pipe logic, we don't save the whole package to fs, otherwise we violate the ulimit.
Downloading or fetching instead of starting

Remove files right after you consume them to conserve memory space
rm -f "$tmpdir/metadata_file"
